newsitem.title: CHINA: GUANGDONG POWER GROUP IN 140 MLN YUAN DEBT ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: GUANGDONG POWER GROUP IN 140 MLN YUAN DEBT ISSUE.

text.p: Guangdong Electric Power Group Co announced on Friday it will issue 140 million yuan ($16.9 million) worth of corporate bonds to finance construction of a power plant.
The three-year bonds, carrying a yield of 11 percent, would be launched on August 18 and finalised on September 7, the company said in an announcement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
China Southern Securities Co would be the lead underwriter, it said, adding that the bonds would be issued at par at 1,000 yuan and 5,000 yuan each.
Beijing has vowed to further expand its power industry by allowing more power suppliers to issue shares or bonds to ease a shortage of funds facing the industry.
Guangdong Power said it would use the proceeds to construct a 3.219 billion yuan power plant in the southwestern province of Yunnan.
Guangdong Power would hold a 30 percent stake in the plant which would have two generators with capacity of 300 megawatts each, the statement said.
The two generators would begin commercial operation in 1998 and 1999, respectively.
The net assets of Guangdong Power are valued at 33.57 billion yuan, the statement said.

The group, which controls a number of power firms in the southern province of Guangdong, including Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd, posted aggregated profits of 3.89 billion yuan between 1993 and 1995.
Sales totalled 47.68 billion yuan during the three-year period, the statement said.

China currently has a total of 25 listed power companies, including 22 listed in either Shanghai or Shenzhen. Chinese power firms listed outside China are the Huaneng International Power Co, the Shandong Huaneng Power Development Co and the Beijing Datang Power Generation Co.
The total assets of the 22 domestically-listed power firms are valued at more than 30 billion yuan, and they raised more than 10 billion yuan in share issue proceeds, state media have said.
